s1.syndrome_frame: Acute, severe chest pain with radiating pain and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm
Broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5 on initial ECG
key_facts: Patient presented with approximately 20 minutes of acute, severe precordial chest pain
Chest pain radiated to the left arm
Patient experienced dyspnea, dizziness, and sweating
Patient has a medical history of hypertension, cerebral infarction, diabetes, and nicotine addiction
Blood pressure was 188/101 mm Hg
Heart rate was 84 beats/min
Respiratory rate was 20 breaths/min
Serum cardiac troponin I level was <0.05 ng/mL
Potassium level was 4.1 mEq/L
Initial ECG showed a sinus rhythm with broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5
Subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery was found on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by dyspnea, dizziness, and sweating, and coronary angiography showed subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and ECG findings are consistent with unstable angina, and the presence of subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Prinzmetal's angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of acute, severe chest pain at rest, accompanied by ECG changes, are consistent with Prinzmetal's angina, and the presence of coronary artery spasm is a possible cause

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with acute, severe chest pain, ECG changes, and coronary angiography findings are consistent with acute coronary syndrome

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of acute, severe chest pain at rest, accompanied by ECG changes, are consistent with variant angina, and the presence of coronary artery spasm is a possible cause

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by dyspnea, dizziness, and sweating, which are classic symptoms of acute coronary syndrome. The initial ECG showed broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5, and coronary angiography revealed subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Serum cardiac troponin I level was within normal range, making acute myocardial infarction less likely

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with unstable angina, the presence of ECG changes and coronary angiography findings suggest a more specific diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG changes are not typical of Prinzmetal's angina, which is characterized by recurrent episodes of chest pain at rest

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG changes are not consistent with variant angina, which is characterized by chest pain at rest with transient ST-segment elevation on ECG
